ai.title: CLI clamps credentials.json and config dir to owner-only permissions
ai.summary: The CLI now writes `credentials.json` with mode `0o600` and creates the config directory with mode `0o700` in `cli/src/utils/auth.ts`, so the bearer token stored in `credentials.json` is restricted to owner read/write on POSIX systems. Because `writeFileSync` only applies `mode` when creating a file, a new `tightenCredentialsFileMode` helper runs `fs.chmodSync` after each write and again on read inside `getUserCredentials`, so existing installs with a umask-wide file are repaired on the next launch. The chmod is skipped on Windows (where POSIX mode bits do not apply) and wrapped in try/catch so a failed chmod never costs a user their login.
ai.evidence: In `cli/src/utils/auth.ts`, the diff adds two constants `CREDENTIALS_FILE_MODE = 0o600` and `CONFIG_DIR_MODE = 0o700`, and applies them in `saveUserCredentials` (via `writeFileSync` { mode } and `mkdirSync` { mode: CONFIG_DIR_MODE }) and `clearUserCredentials` (via `writeFileSync` { mode }), plus a new `tightenCredentialsFileMode` helper that calls `fs.chmodSync` after each write and on every read inside `getUserCredentials`.

ai.title: Foreign client detection adds harness tool names and system prompt markers
ai.summary: common/src/constants/foreign-client-signals.ts now enforces a third layer against request laundering: a request that offers a tool name only a third-party harness ships (Claude Code's `Bash`/`Read`, Codex's `exec_command`, opencode's `webfetch`, etc.) is marked foreign regardless of any genuine Freebuff tool definitions it appends, and a system-role message carrying `You are Claude Code` or `cc_version=` is likewise caught. The two new signals (`foreign_tool_names`, `foreign_system_prompt`) join `foreign_toolset` in the new `ENFORCED_SIGNALS` set consumed by `resolveForeignClientDowngrade`, which downgrades eligible requests to `inclusionai/ling-3.0-tiny:free` unless already on that model. The `unrecognisedToolNames` bounded sample is added to `ForeignClientVerdict` for observe-only logging of requests that clear every enforced rule.

ai.summary: Remote agent validation via `@codebuff/sdk`'s `validateAgents` now attaches an `Authorization: Bearer` header derived from the `apiKey` option in `ValidateAgentsOptions`. The CLI hook `cli/src/hooks/use-agent-validation.ts` supplies that key from `getAuthToken()`, so a logged-in CLI behind a shared NAT is admitted on its own per-user budget once the endpoint's per-IP budget is spent while remaining anonymous otherwise. The endpoint `/api/agents/validate` itself is unchanged; only the optional authenticated header is added.
ai.evidence: In `cli/src/hooks/use-agent-validation.ts`, `validateSelectedAgentDefinitions` now passes `apiKey: getAuthToken()` into the `validateAgents` call, and the JSDoc above it was expanded to note that the bearer token lets a logged-in CLI behind a shared NAT get admitted on its own per-user quota once the endpoint's per-IP budget is spent. In `sdk/src/validate-agents.ts`, `ValidateAgentsOptions` gains an optional `apiKey` field documented as defaulting to `CODEBUFF_API_KEY`, and the remote-validation branch builds an `Authorization: Bearer <key>` header from `options.apiKey ?? getCodebuffApiKeyFromEnv()`.

eli5.text: When you (the person using the assistant in their terminal) are logged in and the shared internet connection your computer is on gets crowded, the validation of your chosen agent now travels with your personal login key. This means you will be quietly recognized as yourself instead of being lumped together with everyone else sharing that connection, so you keep your own usage allowance once the shared pool runs out. Nothing about how you type or what you see on screen changes. The assistant still checks your agents exactly as before, just with better priority when it asks the remote service for confirmation.

ai.title: Release launcher verifies download sha256 before extraction and pins
ai.summary: The shared launcher (`cli/release-core/launcher.js`) now resolves an expected sha256 per target from the wrapper's own `binaryChecksums` map or the registry document, and `downloadAndExtract` runs `verifyFileSha256` against the partial archive before gunzipping or extracting it. A new `write-binary-checksums.js` stamps one hex digest per key in `PLATFORM_TARGET_KEYS` into each product package's `package.json` during the release publish job, and `verifyChecksums` fails the publish if any target is missing or malformed, so the launcher fails closed on an unverifiable archive. The package index files (`cli/release/index.js`, `cli/release-staging/index.js`, `freebuff/cli/release/index.js`) now forward `packageJson.binaryChecksums ?? null` into `createLauncher`, and `http.js` adds `evaluateRedirect` plus the `REDIRECT_ALLOWED_HOST_SUFFIXES` allowlist so follow-up redirects may only land on `*.githubusercontent.com` (plus the explicit hosts). This is the snapshot's most user-relevant change because it gates every self-update and install through an npm-trusted checksum rather than the download origin. It is accompanied by three other changes: a CLI trust gate for repository `.agents` directories, a `--trust-agents` opt-in flag and `CODEBUFF_TRUST_AGENT_DIRS` env var wired through `cli-args.ts`/`index.tsx`, SDK exports of `listLocalAgentFiles`, `getDefaultAgentDirs`, and `MCP_CONFIG_FILE_NAME` so hosts can build their own gates, and a documentation section in `docs/agents-and-tools.md`.

ai.title: Direnv steering vars dropped and registry fetch disabled toggle
ai.summary: The CLI's direnv loader now drops any `.envrc`-exported variable matching a steering prefix (`CODEBUFF_`, `FREEBUFF_`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_`, `OVERRIDE_*`, `NODE_OPTIONS`, `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`, `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED`, `SSL_CERT_*`, `BUN_*`, `LD_*`, `DYLD_*`) rather than importing it into the CLI's own `process.env`, emitting one warning that names the ignored keys. The SDK also gains a `disableAgentRegistry` option on `CodebuffClientOptions` that, when set, makes `getAgentRuntimeImpl` return `null` from `fetchAgentFromDatabase` - so unknown agent ids fail as "not found" instead of falling back to `codebuff/<id>@latest` on the public registry, closing the executable-`handleSteps` eval path for hosts that bundle every agent they will ever run. Together these tighten the trust boundary between a repository's environment and the credential-bearing Freebuff process: direnv may no longer reconfigure the launcher or API plane, and a server-embedded runner can refuse registry fallbacks into a code path from a publisher account it never intended to execute.
ai.evidence: cli/src/init/init-direnv.ts adds `STEERING_ENV_VAR_PATTERNS` (a readonly RegExp array with entries for `CODEBUFF_`, `FREEBUFF_`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_`, `OVERRIDE_*`, `NODE_OPTIONS`, `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`, `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED`, `SSL_CERT_*`, `BUN_*`, `LD_*`, `DYLD_*`) and `isSteeringEnvVar()`, and `initializeDirenv()` now collects matching keys into a `dropped` array and skips importing them into `process.env`, emitting a single warning. sdk/src/impl/agent-runtime.ts adds a `disableAgentRegistry?: boolean` parameter and `fetchAgentFromDatabase: byok || disableAgentRegistry ? async () => null : ...`. sdk/src/run.ts adds `disableAgentRegistry?: boolean` to `CodebuffClientOptions` (with a doc comment stating it refuses every agent-registry fetch, failing unknown/missing ids as not found instead of falling back to `codebuff/<id>@latest`) and threads it through `runOnce` into `getAgentRuntimeImpl`.

eli5.text: The Freebuff CLI now blocks repositories from secretly reconfiguring the assistant's core behavior through environment files, and adds a switch that embedded hosts can use to prevent code downloaded from the registry from running inside their process. This affects developers running the assistant locally and server-side hosts that embed Freebuff into their own applications. If a cloned project tries to override the launcher binary path, API endpoint, TLS trust, or trusted publisher list via its.envrc file, those attempts are now silently dropped and logged as a warning instead of taking effect.

eli5.text: The system that tracks how first-party ads are allocated now records more detailed information about why and how each request is routed, how many placement opportunities were considered versus filled, and whether frequency caps or partial fills occurred. This is purely internal telemetry: no ad selection, routing, or billing logic changed, and your ad experience or pricing is unaffected. Engineers and data analysts studying ad delivery cohorts can now distinguish between "traffic that was looked at" and "traffic deliberately not considered" when sizing regional rollouts, but everyday users see no difference.

ai.title: Sponsored acceptance criteria verification contract and determinism
ai.summary: Adds the versioned acceptance-criteria contract and independent verification machinery for sponsored agentic runs under COD-597. The new `common/src/ads/sponsored-acceptance-criteria.ts` module exports ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA_CONTRACT_VERSION = 1 as const, `ACCEPTANCE_CHECK_KINDS`, `AcceptanceCriterion`, `parseAcceptanceCriteriaContract`, `parseReviewAcceptanceCriteria`, `acceptanceCriteriaSha256`, and `mapAdvertiserSuccessCheck`, and is intentionally dependency-free so Next, Convex V8, and Desktop all import it. The new `common/src/ads/sponsored-verification.ts` module exports `SPONSORED_VERIFIER_VERSION = 'sponsored-verifier/1'`, `SPONSORED_VERIFICATION_RUBRIC_VERSION = 'acceptance-criteria/1'`, `evaluateAcceptanceCriteria`, `reduceVerification`, and `VerificationArtifacts`, and performs the deterministic reduction so Desktop, Cloud, and tests cannot disagree on what success means. The new `common/src/ads/sponsored-verifier.ts` module exports `SPONSORED_VERIFIER_AGENT_ID`, `SPONSORED_VERIFIER_LIMITS`, `SPONSORED_VERIFIER_GUIDANCE`, and `runSponsoredVerifier`, and caps verifier runs at 45_000 ms, 8 tool calls, 1_024 output tokens, and 0 microdollars. The new `common/src/ads/sponsored-verification-reporting.ts` module exports `VerificationRollupRow`, `VerificationCoverage`, and `summarizeVerificationCoverage`, and excludes test traffic from live totals. `SponsoredProposalRow` and `SponsoredProposalViewModel` gain `latest_verification` and `acceptance_criteria_sha256`, and the view model now offers a `verify-again` action in committed, `landed`, and `merged` states when a frozen contract exists. The conformance matrix appends VM-37 and VM-38 to assert that frozen criteria expose verify-again while keeping setup guidance unclaimed and that runs with no rubric are explicitly not verifiable.
